anomalies.observed: Q1 (P-MOS, Device:Q_PMOS_GSD) has its source (pin 2) on +5V and its drain (pin 3) on USBC_VBUS_IN. U6 (LTC4412) VIN is USBC_VBUS_IN and SENSE is +5V. The other P-channel power-path devices, Q6 and Q9, are oriented source-to-input and drain-to-load (Q6.2 on +5V, Q6.3 on 5V_switched). Q1 is the reverse of that.
anomalies.expected: For an LTC4412 ideal-diode OR-ing stage, the P-MOS source should be on the input (VIN, USBC_VBUS_IN) and the drain on the load (+5V). Its body diode should then block reverse flow from +5V back to USB VBUS, as the spec's stated purpose of 'reverse current protection' requires.

evidence.quote: USBC_VBUS_IN [High Power] : J3.A4(VBUS,passive) ... Q1.3(D,passive) R11.1(passive) R64.2(2,passive) U25.5(VBUS,passive) U6.1(VIN,power_in)
USB input "OR-ing"/protection circuitry (LTC4412 ideal-diode controller, U6)

anomalies.impact: The P-MOS body diode conducts from the +5V rail back into the USB VBUS input. Reverse-current protection is lost, and the +5V rail can back-feed the USB port, while forward conduction from VBUS to +5V is also impaired.

anomalies.observed: The anodes of three indicator LEDs (D4, D14, D23) sit on net /LED_3.3V_POWER_SW. No other pin is on that net, so nothing supplies it. Every other LED anode in the design is tied to a live rail (D1.2 and D17.2 to +3V3) or to a driven net (LED_3.3V_POWER_NONINV, driven by U34).
anomalies.expected: The anodes of status LEDs should be connected to a supply or driven rail, such as +3V3 or a switched 3.3V source, so the LEDs can illuminate when their cathodes are pulled low.

evidence.quote: /LED_3.3V_POWER_NONINV : D28.2(A,passive) D29.2(A,passive) D30.3(A1,input) D8.2(A,passive) Q10.1(G,input) R58.2(2,passive) U34.4(Y,output) U7.5(OE,input)

anomalies.impact: D4 (PI activity), D14 (Ethernet Y) and D23 (Ethernet G) cannot light, so the status indication for Ethernet and Pi activity is lost.
